https://www.dw.com/en/us-charges-5-peopl.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MfsF The DOJ unsealed the charges one day after DW published an investigation into one of the members of the network, Oemis Romagoza Durruthy Image: vk.ru Advertisement The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has charged five men with working for Russian intelligence to carry out surveillance and plan targeted killings in the United States and Europe . "The men were recruited to carry out attacks and assassinations around the world, including the United States," the DOJ said in the indictment. Yuri Khrameev, 63, and his son, Kirill Khrameev, 27, both Russian nationals; Cuban nationals Oemis Romagoza Durruthy , 35, and Yaidel Delgado Suarez, 35; and Angel Eduardo Castro of Venezuela , 22, were charged with conspiracy to commit financial terrorism. Khrameev, Suarez, and Castro were also charged with conspiracy to commit murder for hire. All the individuals are still at large. The DOJ announced the unsealing of charges against the five individuals one day after DW published an investigation looking into one of the members of the murder plot. The DW investigation identified Romagoza Durruthy as a salsa teacher in Russia who recruited a number of people in 2024 to carry out sabotage across Europe. The agents were mostly from Spanish-speaking countries and had been sent across Europe to commit arson attacks on businesses and military equipment destined for Ukraine. The investigation found that Romagoza Durruthy had been the person who directed them and organized their travels. How a Cuban dance teacher aided Russian sabotage in EU To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video What else did the DOJ say? Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters that the plans included attempts to assassinate a Russian dissident in Washington, DC. According to the DOJ, several people were recruited in the US alone to surveil Russian dissidents, in addition to monitoring civilian and military infrastructure in European countries such as Lithuania . The Justice Department also reported that one recruit was allegedly offered "$40,000 to 'eliminate' or 'disappear' a US resident." Last year, another recruit was allegedly offered $25,000 to kill a person living in Lithuania. Russia has previously denied carrying out such plots on foreign soil, including in the United States. The Russian Embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvp8.text: Figure caption, Watch: Agents seen outside US Congresswoman llhan Omar's home By Kwasi Gyamfi Asiedu Reporting from Washington Published 12 October 2026 US immigration agents have searched the home of Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar as part of a criminal investigation. Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents "executed a judicially authorised search warrant" for the property in the Washington DC area, a US justice department spokesperson said. The search "is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation", the spokesperson said, but no further details were given. The US Congress is currently out of session and it is unclear if Omar was at the home. Omar, a Democrat and outspoken critic of President Donald Trump, described the search on social media as "an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement". Image source, Reuters Image caption, HSI agents loading a box outside the residence "For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns," Omar said in the post. "This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced." Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump said he had "nothing to do" with the justice department's investigation into Omar, while describing her as a "complainer" and a "terrible person". The Republican president said of the Somali-born congresswoman: "She comes from a country that is a non-country. "And then she comes over here and she complains about our Constitution." Omar's communications director, Jacklyn Rogers, called Monday morning's raid "an outrageous abuse of power" by the Trump administration, and said the congresswoman "has done nothing wrong". The nature of the criminal investigation remains unclear. A BBC crew saw several agents at Omar's home, some carrying boxes to a van. News of the search was first reported by Fox News, which said the investigation was about immigration paperwork filed by her late father when Omar was a child. The timing of the raid - 22 days before the November midterm elections, which will decide the balance of power in Congress for the next two years - raised concerns from Omar's fellow Democrats. The justice department has a longstanding policy of refraining from most enforcement action that is "likely to raise an issue or the perception" it is being brought for the purpose of affecting any election or to disadvantage a candidate. Leading Democrats in the House of Representatives said in a statement that Omar had long been targeted with "vile personal attacks and baseless accusations" by Trump. "Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family," they said. Omar's immigration records have been scrutinised in the past by Republicans. and earlier this year, a fellow congresswoman, Nancy Mace of South Carolina, unsuccessfully filed a subpoena for her records. Last month, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told a conservative podcaster "something is going to happen", making allegations of marital fraud against Omar. Separately, the White House's border tsar, Tom Homan, told Fox News that Omar was being investigated for unspecified immigration violations. Omar denied these allegations last month. "I will say it again so it's as clear as possible: I'm not at all worried about these investigations, because they are complete shams," she said in a campaign fundraising email. Image source, Getty Images Trump has previously suggested that Omar "should go back" to Somalia and that she should be deported. US citizenship is required to serve as a member of the House. Omar has responded to Trump's insults and attacks describing them as an "unhealthy and creepy obsession". The president has also singled out the Somali-American community. Last week, he wrote on social media that Minnesota "is being taken over by Somali immigrants" and "the people of Minnesota must fight back". Some Republicans celebrated Monday's search. "Nobody is above the law," said Tom Emmer, who also represents Minnesota in the House. "We look forward to learning more details about this raid and investigation. ACCOUNTABILITY IS COMING!" Omar is the first Somali American elected to the House and she represents a district in the Minneapolis area. She and Michigan Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib were the first Muslim women elected to Congress. Omar won re-election two years ago with 74% of the vote. Senior political leaders in Minnesota have criticised the search. Governor Tim Walz, a fellow Democrat, said: "Americans see this for what it is - President Trump is abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election." Minnesota Senator Tina Smith called it "a transparent attempt to interfere in our elections". https://hvg.hu/vilag/20261109_krakkoi-lo.text: A szombaton történt, hat halálos áldozatot követelő terrortámadás elkövetője a kórházban hunyt el. Meghalt a kórházban a szombati krakkói lövöldözés elkövetője, aki hat emberrel végzett a lengyel város központjában – közölte hétfőn kora reggel az X közösségi oldalon a lengyel rendőrség. A 24 éves merénylő állapota válságos volt, többszörös műtéten esett át, mielőtt a kórházban életét vesztette. Mint arról beszámoltunk, szombat délután egy lengyel elkövető az autójából válogatás nélkül kezdett lövöldözni a krakkói főtéren sétáló emberekre. A támadóval együtt 16-an sebesültek meg a lövöldözésben, a Külügyminisztérium közlése szerint magyar állampolgár nincs az áldozatok között. A támadót a rendőrök meglőtték, majd őrizetbe vették. A lövöldözést terrorcselekménynek minősítették , az elkövető egy szélsőjobboldali nézeteket valló férfi lehet. Később kiderült, hogy a lövöldöző házában három holttestet találtak , vélhetőleg az elkövető 53 éves apjával, 52 éves anyjával és 20 éves húgával is végzett, mielőtt ámokfutásba kezdett. A támadást később terrorcselekménynek minősítették. Vasárnap délután újabb részletek derültek ki a tömeggyilkosságról. A hat halálos áldozat közül négyen lengyelek (47, 53, illetve 61 éves nők, valamint egy 50 éves férfi). Egy 32 éves brit férfi és egy 51 éves osztrák nő is életét vesztette a támadásban. A sérültek között van az a két rendőr is, aki ártalmatlanította a gyilkost. Egyikük állapota súlyos, a másiké stabil. A merénylő lakásában hét lőfegyvert találtak és foglaltak le. A tettes, valamint az apja is egy lövészklub tagjai voltak, és volt fegyvertartási engedélyük. A merénylet miatt több lengyelországi városban, köztük Varsóban, Gdanskban, Lublinban és Wroclawban megerősítették a rendőri jelenlétet, valamint úttorlaszokat helyeztek ki a köztereken. Vasárnap éjféltől pedig országos, kétnapos nemzeti gyászt hirdettek. Hat halálos áldozata van a lengyelországi Krakkóban szombaton történt terrortámadásnak. A merénylő állapota válságos. Budapesten és Pest megyében több helyszínen zajlanak elfogások és házkutatások egy embercsempész ügyben.
